maria: quick status - i ran a short perf sweep for a fused dequant path that uses a KV-stride heuristic (stride=16) to pack INT4 keys into FP8-friendly lanes. memory looks promising but got quality spikes on long histories.
kevin: nice. which model / seq len and batch?
sam: curious about the spike pattern — prefix length where it diverges?
maria: tested on redwood-open-7b, seq=2048, batch=8. spikes show up after ~1200 tokens for some prompts. avg latency down 9-12% and mem ~11% lower.
jyoti: did you compare with fallback to non-fused dequant? maybe KVC cache alignment problem.
maria: yes — two configs: fused-dequant (kv-stride packing) vs baseline per-token dequant. baseline has stable loss but higher mem. fused variant fails ~0.6% of eval prompts with token-level anomalies.
kevin: can you paste a minimal repro (logs + failing prompt)? also we need to capture the safety signal — what metric flips?
maria: attaching inline snippet of the offending log:```
[run] prompt_id=xyz
model=redwood-open-7b
seq=2048
batch=8
kv_stride=16
step=1234
attn_dequant_mean_diff=0.023
kv_misalignment_warn=true
output_divergence=1.8e-2
```
sam: ok attn_dequant_mean_diff looks small but output_divergence 1.8e-2 is big enough to change next-token distribution. is the misalignment flag deterministic?
maria: it's set when (key_offset % stride) != 0 during chunking. we saw it happen for ~3% of requests due to mixed prefix segmenting (system/message/user boundaries).
jyoti: that suggests the runtime's prefix-splitting logic needs to be stride-aware. we either: (A) avoid packing across segment boundaries, (B) pad keys to stride alignment, or (C) detect and fall back to safe dequant for that request. tradeoffs?
kevin: A is conservative and low-risk but reduces packing efficiency. B increases memory usage slightly and requires zero-copy pad handling. C is simplest to implement quickly but means more unpredictable fallbacks.
sam: also consider a soft-safety signal: run quick cheap checksum on packed vs non-packed attention outputs for first N tokens, if mismatch > threshold trigger fallback and emit telemetry. That lets us stay fast for most requests.
maria: i prototyped checksum-on-first-16-tokens. false positives ~0.2%, true positives caught all observed regression cases. cost is ~3% extra compute on first chunk.
jyoti: good. we should define a safety policy:   - threshold = 1e-3 on KL or L2 between packed vs safe path outputs   - run for first chunk only   - if triggered, switch to baseline per-token dequant and increment a counter for rollout-metrics
kevin: how about rollout strategy? canary at 10% traffic, monitor divergence rate and pct-fallback, then 50% if stable. also expose model-level config to pin stride per-model.
maria: agreed. also need a kernel selection hook: runtime should query kv_stride_compatible(model, request) and return one of {packed, pad-align, fallback}. implement as kernel capability flags + quick predicate.
sam: remember to include a fallback reason code in traces, e.g., DEQUANT_BAD_ALIGNMENT or SAFETY_CHECK_FAIL. helps ops triage.
jyoti: i want an eval harness run across long-dialog benchmarks (>=4096) to validate pack/pad tradeoffs. i'll schedule overnight job.
maria: noted. i'll add the checksum proto to the fused path and instrument telemetry.
runtime-bot: deploy canary started for fused-dequant-kvstride v0.2 -> 10% traffic (canary id: cd-8173).
kevin: cool. after canary we should run a regression alert if fallback_rate > 1% or quality_regression_count > 0.1% of requests.
sam: final ask: add a small CLI flag for local reproduce: `--kv-stride=16 --safety-check=on` so engs can debug easily.
maria: i'll draft the PR and RFC follow-up with perf numbers and safety policy. expected PR tomorrow.
jyoti: can you include a tiny diagram of chunking vs stride in the RFC? helps reviewers.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
